turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his actions were not a threat, but a statement of fact, and that he had been documenting the instances of oppression against his tenantry, and would not hesitate to take further action if necessary.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if his documentation of the instances of oppression would be made public.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and said that Nikhil's documentation was about as thrilling as a list of crop yields, and that he should consider a career change to a more exciting line of work.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant remark was unbecoming of a zamindar and that he should focus on addressing the grievances of the tenantry rather than mocking the efforts of his fellow landowners.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil how he thought his actions would affect the Mussulmans, and whether he believed violence was the only way to address their grievances.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and said that Nikhil's seriousness was almost as amusing as his documentation, and that he was starting to think the Mussulmans were the least of his problems, considering Nikhil's ability to make even the most mundane tasks sound like a call to arms.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his flippant attitude would not deter him from fulfilling his duty to protect the interests of the tenantry, and that he would not be swayed by personal animosity or petty squabbles.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if he thought it was wise to provoke Nikhil further, considering the weight of his words.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was wasting his breath if he thought he could scare him with tales of Mussulman aggression, and that he had more pressing concerns, like his wife's persistent requests for a new bungalow.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that the interests of the tenantry were not something to be taken lightly, and that he would not be swayed by frivolous concerns or personal whims.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala inquired of Nikhil whether his concerns about the Mussulmans were rooted in any concrete evidence, or if they were merely speculative.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and asked Nikhil if he had any other thrilling tales of Mussulman dacoits to regale him with, or if he had simply exhausted his repertoire of scare stories.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the tenantry's safety was not a matter for jest, and that he expected Sandip to take his warnings seriously.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had considered the possibility of a peaceful resolution to the issue with the Mussulmans, and if he had explored any diplomatic channels to address the concerns of both parties.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was not some timid villager cowering in fear of every rustling leaf, and that he would not be swayed by Nikhil's melodramatic warnings.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the zamindari's reputation was at stake and that he would not tolerate any negligence on Sandip's part regarding the security of the tenantry.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if his dismissal of Nikhil's warnings was not a sign of a deeper issue, and if he had considered the potential consequences of his actions on the tenantry and the zamindari's reputation.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil was not the only one who knew how to handle a few scowling Mussulmans, and besides, he had more pressing concerns than indulging in Nikhil's theatrics.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil asked Sandip if he was prepared to accept the consequences of his actions, should the zamindari's reputation be compromised by his inaction.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala inquired of Nikhil, if he truly believed that the zamindari's reputation was at stake, was it not also his responsibility to provide evidence of the potential threat, rather than simply making assertions.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
